editorial.mission: Turn real needs into executable projects by bringing together technology, teams, resources and local partners.
editorial.vision: A connected project network where regional strengths can meet scarce resources in target markets.
editorial.model: Start with demand, match capabilities and trusted counterparts, then coordinate a practical path to delivery. Each project has its own scope and verification needs.
editorial.tech: From hardware and sensors to cloud platforms, edge inference and AI agents, technology helps teams coordinate and build practical systems.
editorial.harlingBio: Harling Sun is a technology architect and business integrator with around 30 years of experience. He founded and led the eBay China API team; his work spans cross-border systems, AI, IoT and platform architecture.
editorial.harlingDetail: The Japan–China AI video brief identifies Harling as the technical partner responsible for the platform architecture. The MOTA project brief describes his wider technology background.
editorial.harlingSkills: His stated technical scope includes AI agents, LLM workflows, IoT, edge computing, cloud infrastructure, data systems and cross-border integration.
editorial.harlingExperience: The supplied briefs also describe work at KONAMI and on IBM financial systems, and architecture for the Shanghai 1210 cross-border service system.
editorial.franklinBio: Franklin Ng is included in the founder introduction. His detailed role, biography and portrait are pending approved materials.
editorial.portfolioNote: Initiatives in progress, not claims of completed delivery or commercial results.
editorial.casesNote: Selected technology showcases; product status and commercial relationships require further verification.

projects.name: ELMSFLOW
projects.summary: Cross-border market entry and local execution for Chinese suppliers and investors.

overview.title: From opportunity discovery to local execution
overview.body: ELMSFLOW connects Chinese suppliers and investors with opportunities in Western markets, then helps organise the practical route to landing: local counterparties, sites, government liaison, compliance pathways and setup.
points: Connects supply and investment capabilities with identified market opportunities.
Coordinates local partners, site options and execution steps.
The Ireland Gateway deck is an example of the landing-support model, not a claim of completed projects.

capabilities.title: Market entry
capabilities.body: Shape an entry route around the target market, intended customer and supplier readiness.

capabilities.title: Local landing
capabilities.body: Organise counterparties, site considerations, government liaison and setup as a practical sequence.

capabilities.title: Compliance readiness
capabilities.body: Map certification and market-access steps with relevant local specialists; requirements must be confirmed with the appropriate authorities.

capabilities.title: Current pipeline
capabilities.body: The project brief identifies food packaging printing, medical/pharmaceutical packaging, factory and warehouse construction, and cold storage as current areas under development. None is presented as completed or approved.

projects.name: Auraight
projects.summary: A bilingual coordination layer for cross-border medical-care pathways.

overview.title: Cross-border care coordination
overview.body: The current project notes describe an independent bilingual coordination layer connecting Shanghai and Japan with patient-development pathways across North America, the UK, Nigeria, Singapore, Thailand and New Zealand. This is a coordination concept, not a clinical provider or a treatment-outcome claim.
points: Shanghai and Japan are the named resource locations in the current project notes.
The notes list international patient pathways across six regions.
No clinical outcomes or specific hospital relationships are asserted in this deck.

capabilities.title: Patient coordination
capabilities.body: Coordinate enquiries and cross-border next steps around the patient's requested pathway; clinical decisions remain with qualified providers.

capabilities.title: Shanghai and Japan resources
capabilities.body: The project notes identify Shanghai hospital resources and high-end medical resources in Japan; institution names and service details remain to be confirmed.

capabilities.title: Screening pathways
capabilities.body: Screening and overseas checks are listed as areas of coordination, not as guaranteed services or medical outcomes.

capabilities.title: Bilingual navigation
capabilities.body: A bilingual coordination layer is intended to help patients navigate cross-border communication and logistics.

projects.name: VFlux
projects.summary: A proposed network layer for global asset distribution, liquidity, routing and clearing.

overview.title: Connect assets, venues and investors
overview.body: The VFLUX project material describes a multi-asset infrastructure layer connecting eligible asset providers, trading venues and investors through distribution, liquidity coordination, routing, clearing and settlement. The source describes an initial centralised operating model, with any on-chain progression staged over time.
points: Designed to connect specialist institutions rather than replace them.
Market access, participant permissions and partner connections are part of the described role.
This is a project description; it is not a representation of regulatory approval or live trading.

capabilities.title: Asset access and distribution
capabilities.body: Organise an asset directory, admission criteria, investor eligibility, product permissions and distribution-channel connections.

capabilities.title: Routing and liquidity
capabilities.body: Coordinate routing and shared liquidity across participating venues and distribution channels.

capabilities.title: Clearing and settlement
capabilities.body: Provide a network-level coordination layer for clearing, reconciliation and settlement between participants.

capabilities.title: Institutional roles
capabilities.body: The source distinguishes VFLUX's network role from the specialist responsibilities of regulated and professional counterparties.

projects.name: 吉晟株式会社 · YOSHI SEI CORPORATION
projects.summary: Japan–China AI video production matching and transaction platform; website beta is in development.

overview.title: A Japan–China production bridge
overview.body: The supplied Yoshisei project brief describes a Japan-based platform connecting Japanese buyers with Chinese AI video studios. It proposes fair matching and a workflow covering production, Japanese localisation, agreed quality checks and JPY–RMB settlement. The brief says the website beta is in development; planned activity is not presented as completed.
points: The brief identifies 吉晟株式会社 / YOSHI SEI CORPORATION and a Tokyo headquarters with Osaka and Fukuoka branches.
AI short animation / manga IP is the lead category, with AI advertising and education as adjacent categories.
First transactions are planned for January–March 2027 in the brief; this is a plan, not achieved traction.

capabilities.title: Buyer and studio matching
capabilities.body: Translate buyer briefs into production requirements and match them with Chinese AI production partners.

capabilities.title: Production workflow
capabilities.body: The brief maps coverage across planning, scripting, generation, storyboarding, direction, editing, visual work and delivery.

capabilities.title: Japanese localisation and review
capabilities.body: Localise the deliverable and check it against mutually agreed Japanese-language quality criteria before acceptance.

capabilities.title: Cross-border settlement
capabilities.body: The proposed flow is JPY collection and RMB settlement to the studio after acceptance, subject to the agreed transaction and applicable requirements.
